source.title: The Kinetics of Training: A Driven-Nucleation Rate Law for Emergence, Plasticity Loss, and Circuit Control in Language Models

page_placements.theme: Redundancy and shifting identity of induction heads; distribution depends on architecture

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study measures induction-mechanism and task-skill timing, and reports that the mechanism, in-context learning, and strict copying do not all arrive at one identical step. This refines the single-transition account, although the paper does not test every part of the claim’s loss-curve description.
record.gate_note: The paper also cites induction-head findings from prior work; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Its own measurements of induction scores, timing, ablations, and training-data changes are included. The reported smooth validation-loss decrease is during aging/plasticity loss, not a measurement of the training-loss bump at induction emergence.
record.test_reason: The study measures induction heads in Pythia and OLMo with its own probes and ablations. It reports a prefix-matching induction score, a previous-token precursor, the onset of ICL relative to the mechanism, and data-mix and aging effects on whether induction forms. This is a different method aimed at the same questions. It does not reproduce the attention-only setup or the loss bump.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is too narrow. The authors conclude that one nucleation rate equation (sites x attempts x drive x e^-betaK, minus destruction) governs capability formation. Read forward, it gives an emergence floor, a throttle, and a precursor clock that predicts induction onset to a median 5%. Read backward, it gives loss of plasticity through attention-head occupation, repaired by a QK reset. With an injected temperature, it allows control of circuits. The staged ordering of mechanism, ICL and copying is a supporting observation, not the main conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures induction behavior and onset on public checkpoints and uses a different rate-law framework; it does not reproduce the original attention-only training experiment or its loss-curve measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with model size and capacity: the few-shot label-induction skill is absent through 143k steps at 70M, late at 160M, and earlier at 410M and 1B. Data-mix concentration and switch timing also affect ignition.

fits_no_version.finding: Across seven capabilities, single-part ablation leaves a median 16.7% of capability (32/32 cells below partial credit), while random non-part ablation leaves 100%. Results are pooled.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Real-model circuits near ignition behave conjunctively under single-part ablation.

fits_no_version.finding: Strict exact-copy behaviour lags the induction mechanism by x1.27.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different behaviours that use induction heads arrive at different times after the mechanism forms.

fits_no_version.finding: At late checkpoints of 410M and 1B, no single head is necessary for copying (0.95 retained); redundancy grows with scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction-type copy circuits delocalize into redundant copies later in training and at larger scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Under injected weight noise, the previous-token head melts at 5.3–6.4x the induction head's threshold, at every Pythia scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The composed induction circuit is more fragile than its precursor part.

record.code_released: not stated; the text says per-experiment JSON files and scripts are released but gives no URL
record.problems: The induction-head timing evidence is based on checkpoint probes rather than a direct causal test of the proposed composition. The paper does not report the training-loss bump or establish a narrow formation window. Evidence covers two families and models up to 1.4B, and several reported model-level results are aggregates. Some causal training results use small run counts, as noted in the paper.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant numeric outcomes were left out. Related results about plasticity loss, injected-temperature control, and other capabilities were excluded where they did not measure one of the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Small attention-only transformers. The composition operation (K-composition through QK) is not causally isolated.
Abruptness or narrowness of the formation window. Coincidence with a training-loss bump.
Whether induction heads cause most ICL in large models. There is no separate causal estimate; ICL co-onset is correlational.
Families beyond Pythia and OLMo, sizes above 1.4B, other architectures and modalities.
Data properties other than repeated-token concentration (e.g. burstiness, distributional properties). Persistence of ICL.
Which other heads or mechanisms carry few-shot learning; no ablation comparison is made.
Whether induction-head formation itself consists of several sub-transitions. Only precursor-then-induction ordering and behaviour lags are reported.

missing.what: Concentration floor for induction formation: 0/12 ignite at c<=0.26 vs 4/5 at 0.28 (70M). The floor falls with scale, and the dose throttle runs never/~1400/~470 steps.
OLMo-1B switch: control 0/2, switch 2/2 at ~247 steps, delayed switch taxed (471/799)
Aging tax and horizon: delay 506→1108→1115 steps; no ignition at S=3600; horizon grows with scale. QK-only reset restores induction 6/6 (score 0.700) vs OV 0/6 (0.252).
Previous-token precursor dates induction onset (C=1.241; 6/6 held-out models, median 5% error; OLMo-1B 1.244)
Fresh sites must be opened in pairs across both layers for induction to re-form; single-layer openings 0/6

record.verdict_notes: V1 evidence comes from Pythia, which has MLPs, not from attention-only models. The V7 label was removed because the reader's V7 verdict cited R6 (not linked to V7), and R5 and R7 do not measure sub-steps of induction formation. The few-shot label-induction rows were relinked from V4 to V6: they measure a task skill, not induction heads. The paper's toy EK-1 result (memoryless, single-barrier waiting) concerns synthetic conjunction circuits, not induction heads.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures induction behavior and identifies previous-token and induction heads as the necessary set in early checkpoints, but does not causally isolate the proposed composition operation in a small attention-only transformer.

The study reports relative onset of mechanism and in-context learning, but not whether induction-head formation occurs in a narrow window or whether it coincides with a bump in the training-loss curve.

The study does not establish that induction heads cause most in-context learning in large transformers. It reports timing and aggregate circuit-ablation results, but not a separated causal estimate of induction heads’ contribution to most in-context learning.
Evidence is limited to Pythia and OLMo, models up to 1.4B parameters, and the reported checkpoints and training setups; other model families, modalities, and architectures are not tested.
The data-mix and timing interventions concern the paper’s repeated-token capability setup; they do not map dependence across all data properties or training regimes.
The study does not compare induction heads with alternative mechanisms as carriers of few-shot task learning.
The study measures a staged ordering of mechanism, task behavior, and strict copying, but does not determine whether all induction-head formation consists of multiple distinct sub-transitions.
